'''Hoth Limited''' is the 7th expansion of Star Wars CCG, published by Decipher in November 1996.<ref name="decexp">[https://web.archive.org/web/19990504174938/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Star Wars CCG: The Expansions], Decipher.com (archive, 4 May 1999)</ref> It is 162 cards (81 Light Side and 81 Dark Side): 54 rares, 54 uncommons, and 54 commons.<ref name="deccards">Decipher.com card lists: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/light/index.html Hoth Light Side] and [https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/index.html Hoth Dark Side] (archive, 11 June 2002); [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists] (archive, 25 December 2008); [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007).</ref> The expansion symbol is the planet Hoth.

This was the first set drawn from ''The Empire Strikes Back''. It introduced the "persona" mechanic, [[AT-AT]] walkers and the Hoth Energy Shield Rules. A persona is a second version of a main character with different abilities, such as [[Commander Luke Skywalker]] and [[Luke Skywalker]]. Under the Energy Shield Rules, the Dark Side cannot deploy on the first four marker Hoth sites or interior Hoth sites unless [[Hoth: Main Power Generators (1st Marker)|Main Power Generators]] is "blown away". There were no Hoth starter decks; the related [[The Empire Strikes Back Introductory Two-Player Game]] followed shortly after. The set went out of print in September 1998 when Revised Unlimited (white border) replaced it.<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2] Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009141805/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]. [https://www.starwarsccg.org/collecting/ SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia] at starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261022023930/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/collecting.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="wook">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Hoth_Limited Hoth Limited] Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20190819212836/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Hoth_Limited Internet Archive] at Wookieepedia</ref>

== Packaging ==
Limited Edition was sold in 15-card booster packs (MSRP $3: 10 commons, 4 uncommons, 1 rare, plus a Decipher ad insert) and 36-pack booster boxes.<ref name="encyc" />

== Memorabilia ==
Decipher issued a four-panel poster (~32&Prime; &times; 10.5&Prime;) for every expansion from Premiere through Death Star II. Premiere's reverse is blank; later sets, including Hoth, print that expansion's card list on the back.<ref name="encyc" />

[[File:Hoth-Limited-four-panel-poster.png|720px|Hoth Limited four-panel poster front]]

''Front''

[[File:Hoth-Limited-four-panel-poster-back.png|480px|Hoth Limited four-panel poster reverse]]

''Reverse (Light Side / Dark Side card list)''

Limited packs included a two-panel Decipher ad insert (website, FTP, faxback, and EMailBack). The booster ''box'' held the fold-out Hoth Rules Supplement, with new rules on one side and the full card list on the other. The rules covered location deployment, the Hoth Energy Shield, missing, enclosed vehicles and related changes.<ref name="encyc" />

== Print sheets ==
Per side the rare sheet is 8&times;10 (80 cards): 15 R1s twice, 12 R2s four times, and two unused slots. Uncommons are 12&times;13 (156 cards): 15 U1s four times and 12 U2s eight times. Commons are 10&times;10 (100 cards): 5 C1s twice, 21 C2s four times, and one C3 ([[Echo Base Trooper]] / [[Snowtrooper]]) six times.<ref name="encyc" />

Hoth is the first expansion whose rare sheets leave two blank slots. Those slots were printed solid black or left white, with a Light or Dark card back; six combinations are known. Most blanks were pulled after cutting, but some reached packs. They are not playable and are not counted in the 162-card set.<ref name="encyc" />

== Variants ==
Limited [[R-3PO (Ar-Threepio)|R-3PO]] was printed with [[K-3PO (Kay-Threepio)|K-3PO]]'s picture. Decipher ran a redemption: send in the wrong card, receive a shrink-wrapped corrected copy. About 110,000 incorrect copies were printed; returned cards were destroyed so the total print run would stay the same.<ref name="encyc" />

{| class="wikitable" style="background:transparent; border:none;"
|- style="background:transparent; vertical-align:top;"
| style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Hoth-Limited-R-3PO-misprint.png|180px|R-3PO with K-3PO artwork]]<br />''Misprint (K-3PO art)''
| style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Hoth-Limited-R-3PO-corrected.png|180px|Corrected R-3PO]]<br />''Corrected version''
|}

Some copies of [[Turn It Off! Turn It Off!]] add a "0" after the last quotation in the lore (<code>TURN IT OFF!"0</code>). It may be a typesetting error or an Easter egg for "off" in binary.<ref name="encyc" />

[[File:Hoth-Limited-Turn-It-Off-variant.png|280px|Turn It Off! lore variant with extra 0]]

== Other printings ==
'''Revised Unlimited''' (white border) was released in September 1998: 9-card packs (MSRP $2.50: 5 commons, 3 uncommons, 1 rare) in 30-pack boxes, plus a box Rules Supplement. It reprints the Limited pool with Special Edition–era revised text. For example, "Adds 2 to the power of any starship he pilots" became "Adds 2 to the power of anything he pilots".<ref name="encyc" />

'''Japanese Limited''' (black border; 氷の惑星ホス) was released in September 1998: 15-card packs (MSRP ¥500) in 36-pack boxes, with a Japanese Rules Supplement. Rare sheets were collated 3:1 Light to Dark, so Dark rares are scarcer from packs. Uncommons may have been collated about 2:1 Dark to Light. Some Japanese copies of [[Snowtrooper Officer]] and [[E-web Blaster]] were printed without a card title.<ref name="encyc20">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/SWCCG+Collecting+Encyclopedia+2.0.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 2.0] Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20200930091918/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/SWCCG+Collecting+Encyclopedia+2.0.pdf Internet Archive], Players Committee, July 2015</ref>

== Easter egg ==
The Mon Calamari Star Cruisers were not available to the Rebellion until mid-way through ''Return of the Jedi''.<ref name="artshow-hoth-limited">[http://www.decipher.com/artshow/eastereggs/starwarsccg/hoth/ehothpackaging.html Hoth Limited], Art Show: Easter Eggs, Decipher.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000509123557/http://www.decipher.com/artshow/eastereggs/starwarsccg/hoth/ehothpackaging.html Internet Archive], 9 May 2000.</ref>
